terms.gloss: for half the price, at half price
terms.grammar: dīmidiō, ablative of the measure of difference, with minōris, genitive of price; with cōnstāre, emere, vēndere, or vēnīre
evidence: Cic. Att. 13.29.1: prope dīmidiō minōris cōnstābit
terms.comment: Latin says “cheaper by half”: dīmidiō measures the difference, and the genitive minōris gives the price, as in plūris and minōris cōnstāre (see “cost a lot”). Cicero writes it of a covered walk that would cost nearly half as much to build at one place as at another. For a sign in a shop, give the discount (see “discount”).

phrases.latin: Hī calceī hodiē dīmidiō minōris vēneunt.
phrases.english: These shoes are half price today.
I got it at half price!

phrases.latin: tēcta igitur ambulātiuncula addenda est; quam ut tantam faciāmus quantam in Tusculānō fēcimus prope dīmidiō minōris cōnstābit istō locō.
phrases.english: So a covered walk must be added; to make it as large as the one we made at Tusculum will cost nearly half as much in that place.

sources: Lewis & Short: dimidius · Lewis & Short: parvus
